subject: Post-call action: throughput vs accuracy trade study for Biosyn integration
messages:
From: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.ai>
To: Amy Chen <amy.chen@biosyn.ai>, Marco Rossi <marco@bioapps.it>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 16:05:00 +0000
Subject: Post-call recap & proposed benchmarks (throughput vs accuracy)

Hi Amy / Marco —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the recommended next steps so we can scope the POC run: 

Key constraints we captured
- Throughput target: ~1.5k summary tokens/sec sustained for batchy ingestion (200–300 requests/sec typical burst)
- Latency SLO: p95 < 350ms for 256-token responses in user-facing summarization endpoints
- Quality bar: extractive summary F1 >= 0.82 on your gold set; low hallucination rate on entity-level checks
- Typical input lengths: 1–5k tokens (mostly docs + metadata), many multi-document prompts
- Data sensitivity: regulated clinical-sounding content; need encryption-in-transit and option for Private deployment (VPC) during benchmarking

Model candidates to include in comparative runs (we will run on Redwood Dedicated):
1) Llama-3-70B-chat (quant variants for throughput) — expected highest quality baseline
2) Instruction-tuned 13B (open 13B inst) — cost/throughput middle ground
3) Mistral-instruct (7B) — best-effort low-cost throughput candidate

Quantization and runtime variants we recommend testing in parallel:
- FP16 baseline (no quant) — quality anchor
- AWQ 4-bit (selective layer-preserve) — best throughput/cost, watch instruction-following regressions
- GPTQ 4-bit (per-channel) — more conservative, sometimes better for factual calibration
- FP8 on supported HW (Ampere/Grace-class) — promising for latency but limited availability

Deliverables we will send / need from you
- We attached a first-pass prompt suite tailored to your summary tasks (biosyn_prompt_suite_v1.json) — please confirm this is representative.
- We'll provide benchmark links and dashboards (Drive + HubSpot links in this thread).
- Ask: please confirm we have permission to run benchmarks on redwood dedicated capacity and any NDA constraints on storing sample outputs.

Next steps / proposed timeline
- You confirm prompt suite and NDA constraints (this week)
- Redwood runs 3-day comparative runs (FP16, AWQ 4-bit, GPTQ 4-bit) over your gold set + synthetic stress inputs (start next Mon)
- Deliver a trade study report with cost/latency/quality tables and recommendations (within 7 business days of run completion)

Attachments: biosyn_prompt_suite_v1.json, quant-trade-study-table.xlsx

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-min slot if preferred.

Rohan Mehta
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
rohan.mehta@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0128

From: Amy Chen <amy.chen@biosyn.ai>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.ai>, Marco Rossi <marco@bioapps.it>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 18:21:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & proposed benchmarks (throughput vs accuracy)

Hi Rohan — thanks for the clear recap. A couple quick clarifying Qs before we sign off on the prompt suite: 

1) For the AWQ 4-bit runs: do you have examples or prior case studies showing the kinds of instruction-following regressions you mentioned? We need to understand the risk to clinical phrasing.
2) On FP8: our infra team is cautious about FP8 for anything production. If it's only for latency experiments that's okay — can you confirm we won't use any outputs for training/evaluations outside the POC?
3) NDA: we have a limited POC NDA in place (I'll attach to the HubSpot record). For storage, Biosyn requires sample outputs to be deleted from vendor systems after 30 days unless we agree otherwise. Is that doable?

Confirming we authorize Redwood to run the Dedicated benchmark once we sign and exchange the redlined POC NDA. Also looping Marco for the infra constraints (we might be limited to GCP-A region).

Best,
Amy Chen
Head of Product
Biosyn Therapeutics
amy.chen@biosyn.ai | +1 (650) 444-8822

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Amy Chen <amy.chen@biosyn.ai>, Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 09:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & proposed benchmarks (throughput vs accuracy)

Thanks Amy — quick answers and concrete baselines from our side.

1) AWQ regressions: we observed three typical failure modes in instruction workloads when going from FP16 -> AWQ 3/4-bit aggressive configs:
   - Reduced instruction-following fidelity on rare control tokens (prompts that use bespoke separators or explicit style tokens)
   - Slightly higher propensity to hallucinate for long-context multi-document synthesis unless KV cache precision is preserved for the later transformer layers
   - Numeric drift on tight entity extraction tasks (dates/IDs) in lowest quant levels
We have an internal case study (not public) comparing AWQ 4-bit selective-preserve vs full 4-bit that I can share under NDA; link added to Drive folder.

2) FP8 usage: agreed — we'll mark FP8 runs as "experiment-only" and we will not export those outputs outside the POC analysis. We can commit to your 30-day deletion requirement for any sample outputs stored on Redwood side.

3) Region / infra: Redwood Dedicated has a GCP-A pool available; Monica can confirm exact GPU SKUs and whether FP8 paths can be exercised there.

Suggested baseline metrics to capture (we'll run automated + human eval):
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 token and full-response
- Throughput: sustained tokens/sec under the expected request mix
- Cost: $/1k tokens for each model+quant config (inc. infra amortized)
- Quality: extractive F1, ROUGE-L, hallucination rate (entity-level), and a 200-sample human preference set

We will prepare the benchmark-run-template.md so you see the exact steps and metrics. Proposed quick timeline: drive runs Mon–Wed next week, sync Thurs for preliminary results.

Link: https://drive.redwood.internal/drive/folders/BIOSYN-POC-2027 (private link)

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

[Attachment: benchmark-run-template.md]

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Amy Chen <amy.chen@biosyn.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Aug 2027 09:42:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & proposed benchmarks (throughput vs accuracy)

Hi all — adding the quantization trade-offs matrix and a recommended test plan. Summary first:

Short summary (quick read)
- AWQ 4-bit (selective preserve): best cost/throughput. Risk: medium for instruction-following on edge prompts. Mitigation: preserve top N layers in FP16, include human eval on style prompts.
- GPTQ 4-bit (per-channel): slightly lower throughput than AWQ, but lower quality regression risk on entity fidelity. Good middle-ground.
- FP8 (hardware-dependent): highest latency improvement on supported HW; availability may be limited in the GCP-A pool. Use only for latency experiments, not quality anchor.

Estimated delta vs FP16 baseline (approx for your workload):
- AWQ 4-bit: latency -45% p95, cost -62%, expected quality drop on strict entity metrics: -3 to -6 pts F1 (depends on prompt set)
- GPTQ 4-bit: latency -30% p95, cost -45%, quality drop: -1 to -3 pts F1
- FP8: latency -50% p95 (hw permitting), cost -55%, quality delta: variable, requires validation

Recommended test plan (minimum to make a go/no-go decision)
1) Baseline FP16 on Llama-3-70B-chat (2 days) — establish quality anchor and infra numbers
2) GPTQ 4-bit run on same model (1 day) — check entity fidelity and hallucination rate
3) AWQ 4-bit selective-preserve (1 day) — evaluate throughput gains vs human-eval drop
4) Mistral-7B FP16 + AWQ 4-bit runs (1 day) — low-cost option baseline

We will attach the trade study spreadsheet (quant-trade-study-table.xlsx) with the full expected metrics and measurement formulas. Action items for Biosyn: sign POC NDA with 30-day sample deletion clause; confirm GCP-A availability and whether sampling on live-prod traffic is allowed (we assume no).

I can schedule an ops-run call for Monday 08/16 09:00 PT to lock the GPU SKUs and finalize telemetry instrumentation (tracing + token breakdown). Are you available?

Monica Patel
Platform Performance Lead, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai | +1 (646) 555-0442
